items.quote: Onimusha: Way of the Sword is easily a contender for game of the year, as it blends merciless action with skill-based combat in a near-seamless way. The story and visuals complement the ridiculously sharp gameplay extremely well, and though the camera can be a little problematic on rare occasions, that shouldn’t stop you from experiencing Capcom’s latest banger.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword is a visually stunning revival that successfully brings Capcom’s classic franchise into the modern era using the RE Engine. Musashi injects a refreshing sense of personality into dark fantasy Kyoto, especially during the game’s intense and cinematic boss fights. This is definitely an action adventure game of the year contender.
As rewarding as it is difficult, Onimusha isn’t just one of the best games of the year; it’s one of the best action games ever made.

For as long as I can remember, I have wanted to be perfect for 10 seconds. Onimusha: Way of the Sword understands that desire. Each time I landed a perfectly timed Issen, pulled off a risky deflect, or landed a combo at just the right time, I felt like I had accomplished something. I had put myself to the test, and I’d succeeded. It’s a testament to Way of the Sword’s combat that I could beat it without using some of the systems designed to help you progress – not because you don’t need them, but because it leaves room for you to truly understand its action and overcome their absence through sheer determination. Even if I hadn’t intentionally made things harder for myself, though, I still would have loved spending time with Okuni, Takamura, Murasaki, Shizuka, and nearly all the denizens of this world. I still would have thought that Musashi himself is one of the coolest, most interesting protagonists in any video game, and I would have loved going on this journey with him. I still would have savored the creative fights against Ganryu and Benkei and a dozen others I won’t spoil here. My journey reflected Musashi's, and Onimusha made that possible. The best part of life is the challenge. You have to learn to love the fight.

Onimusha is a criminally underrated series, and while it was not a series I was expecting to be revived, I am delighted to see it make a comeback. And with the sheer quality that Capcom has pumped into Way of the Sword, I have no doubt that this is a game that is going to sell like hotcakes, and I'm already getting my hopes up for another new Onimusha title, In a competitive field, Onimusha: Way of the Sword is hands-down the best action-adventure title of the year so far. Its combat system is as electrifying as it is challenging to master, and it's backed up by a great story and characters, and a lovely little world to explore. Capcom can probably scarcely believe how well its 2026 is going. Here's hoping its new golden age continues for many years to come.

Onimusha is back and ready to claim the highest honors. Content,
quality, fun – the full package is right here.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword marks a triumphant return for Capcom’s samurai action series, combining spectacular visuals with deep, demanding combat built around precise parries, the classic Issen technique, and a varied arsenal of Oni weapons. Strong performances, memorable boss battles, rewarding progression, and an excellent recreation of feudal Japan make it one of Capcom’s most accomplished action games, while repetitive sub-bosses and a few minor presentation issues do little to diminish an outstanding experience.
Onimusha: Way of the Sword proves Capcom can't go wrong in 2026, offering combat that stands out with every swing of the blade and fascinating characters.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword masterfully revives the franchise with gameplay rich in mechanics and variety, full of boss battles that could make even FromSoftware fans envious. The story is like an incredible shonen anime. Musashi is a captivating and funny protagonist, accompanied by a cast of equally interesting supporting characters and antagonists who come together to create one of the best journeys Capcom has ever crafted.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword is such a refreshing action game, with focus on its combat systems and cinematic narrative. In those respects, it sets a high standard for all other video games. The only critiques some could make is that it’s a very linear game, and that could be a problem for some. It’s also maybe 20 hours long, and once the story’s finished, there isn’t a breadth of post-game modes. Onimusha: Way of the Sword is a cinematic action game, and Capcom exceeded any expectations people could have in that regard. It just lacks some kind of score mode, or Bloody Palace to keep players invested beyond the main story. I loved Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and I think it will be celebrated as a modern action classic.
